metadata.name: lsp_activate_tools
metadata.label: Activate choco-pi-lsp Tools
metadata.description:
Activate one or more situational choco-pi-lsp tools that stay registered but inactive by default, so the default tool list stays lean. Call this ONCE with the tools you need before using them — they become callable starting the NEXT turn. Available:
ast_grep_search — AST-aware structural code search across ~40 languages (ast-grep patterns).
ast_grep_replace — AST-aware structural code rewrite/refactor (ast-grep patterns).
ast_grep_outline — Syntax-only file/dir structure (symbols/imports/exports/members) via ast-grep outline — no index/LSP.
ast_grep_dump — Dump the tree-sitter AST for a source snippet to discover node kinds/field names.
lsp_navigation — IDE-style LSP navigation: definition, references, implementation, rename, call hierarchy.
diagnostic_mark — Record a disposition for a diagnostic: false-positive / suppress (inline ignore comment) / defer (this session) / flagged (to fix).
metadata.promptSnippet: Activate situational ast-grep / lsp_navigation tools before using them

tools.description: Names of situational tools to activate (see this tool's description for the catalog).

metadata.name: ast_grep_search
metadata.label: AST Search
metadata.description:
Search code using AST-aware pattern matching. IMPORTANT: Use specific AST patterns, NOT text search.

✅ GOOD patterns (complete AST shapes; $$$ accepts zero or more nodes):
  - function $NAME($$$ARGS) { $$$BODY } (function declaration)
  - fetchMetrics($$$ARGS)             (call with any arguments)
  - import { $$$NAMES } from "module-name" (exact string-literal import)
  - console.log($MSG)                 (method call)

❌ BAD patterns (multiple nodes / raw text):
  - it"test name"                     (missing parens - use it($TEST))
  - console.log without args           (incomplete code)
  - arbitrary text without code structure

Metavariables match AST nodes, not text inside quoted string literals: `from "$PATH"` matches the literal text $PATH. Use an exact quoted string for a known import, or grep for wildcard text. Use 'paths' to scope to specific files/folders. Use 'nodeKind' to find every node of a known AST kind, or 'ast_grep_dump' first when the kind is unknown. Avoid 'selector' unless you know the exact AST node kind; it narrows matching and does not extract fields. If this tool is inactive, call lsp_activate_tools with tools=["ast_grep_search"]; activation takes effect next turn. If zero matches, retry once with a simpler AST pattern, then use ast_grep_dump on a small representative snippet before falling back to grep.

pattern.description: AST pattern (use function/class/call context, not text). Required unless `rule` or `nodeKind` is provided. Do not put metavariables inside quoted string literals; they match literally.

selector.description: Advanced: restrict search to a specific AST node kind (for example 'call_expression' or 'function_declaration'). This narrows matching; it does not extract fields from matches.

context.description: Show N lines before/after each match for context

nodeKind.description: Expert grammar-specific escape hatch: find every node of this exact AST kind (for example `call_expression`) without writing a pattern. Node kinds are not universal across languages; use ast_grep_dump to discover them. Mutually exclusive with `pattern` and `rule`; can be combined with structural constraints.

insideKind.description: Restrict matches to nodes inside an ancestor of this AST node kind. Example: `insideKind: "function_declaration"` finds the pattern only when it appears inside a function body. Searches all ancestors (stopBy: end), not just the immediate parent. Synthesizes a YAML rule — takes precedence over `selector` and `strictness`.

hasKind.description: Restrict matches to nodes whose immediate child has this AST node kind (ast-grep default stopBy: neighbor). Example: `hasKind: "await_expression"`.

hasDescendantKind.description: Restrict matches to nodes containing this AST node kind anywhere in their descendants. Explicit recursive form (`stopBy: end`); use this instead of `hasKind` when nesting is not immediate.

follows.description: Restrict matches to nodes that immediately follow a sibling matching this pattern. Example: `follows: "return $X"` finds the pattern only when preceded by a return statement.

precedes.description: Restrict matches to nodes that immediately precede a sibling matching this pattern.

rule.description: Raw ast-grep YAML rule. When provided, routes through `sg scan --config` instead of `sg run -p`, unlocking the full rule DSL. Takes precedence over `pattern` and structural-intent params. The YAML must include `id` and `language` fields.

skip.description: Match offset for pagination. Skip the first N matches and return the next page. Use when results are truncated — increment by the page size to retrieve subsequent pages.

maxMatches.description: Cap on matches returned per call (default 50, max 200). Lower it to keep a broad search compact; raise it to page less. Also sets the pagination step for skip.

groupByFile.description: Render results grouped by file (one line per file with L<line>:<col> locations) instead of each match's body. Compact distribution view for high-volume searches; match read-slices remain in details.matchLocations.

strictness.description: Pattern matching strictness. 'smart' (default) ignores comments and whitespace. 'relaxed' also ignores unnamed nodes like punctuation — useful when optional trailing commas cause misses. 'ast' ignores all whitespace. 'signature' matches only structural shape, ignoring bodies.

validateOnly.description: Validate/compile the pattern or rule without scanning project files. Helps distinguish a bad pattern/rule from a real no-match result.

metadata.name: ast_grep_replace
metadata.label: AST Replace
metadata.description:
Replace code using AST-aware pattern matching. IMPORTANT: Use specific AST patterns, not text. Dry-run by default (use apply=true to apply).

✅ GOOD patterns (single AST node):
  - pattern='console.log($MSG)' rewrite='logger.info($MSG)'
  - pattern='var $X' rewrite='let $X'
  - pattern='function $NAME() { }' rewrite='' (delete)

❌ BAD patterns (will error):
  - Raw text without code structure
  - Missing parentheses: use it($TEST) not it"text"
  - Incomplete code fragments

Always use 'paths' to scope to specific files/folders. Dry-run first to preview changes.

pattern.description: AST pattern to match (be specific with context)

insideKind.description: Restrict matches to nodes inside an ancestor of this AST node kind. Synthesizes a YAML rule.

hasKind.description: Restrict matches to nodes whose immediate child has this AST node kind (ast-grep default stopBy: neighbor). Example: `hasKind: "await_expression"`.

hasDescendantKind.description: Restrict matches to nodes containing this AST node kind anywhere in their descendants. Explicit recursive form (`stopBy: end`); use this instead of `hasKind` when nesting is not immediate.

follows.description: Restrict matches to nodes that immediately follow a sibling matching this pattern.

precedes.description: Restrict matches to nodes that immediately precede a sibling matching this pattern.

strictness.description: Pattern matching strictness. 'smart' (default) ignores comments and whitespace. 'relaxed' also ignores unnamed nodes like punctuation. 'ast' ignores all whitespace.

metadata.name: ast_grep_outline
metadata.label: AST-Grep Outline
metadata.description:
Syntax-only code structure (symbols, imports, exports, and members) via `ast-grep outline`. Fast, local, no index/LSP/cross-file semantics — useful for languages or structures where choco-pi-lsp's own extractor is weak, or for a raw second opinion.

Prefer module_report for choco-pi-lsp-aware navigation (who-uses-this, complexity/fanout, recommendedReads, blast radius, callback handles). Use ast_grep_outline when you want the syntax tree's own view of a file or a whole directory.

Returns JSON: per file, `items[]` with name/symbolType/signature/range, `isExported`/`isImport`, nested `members[]` (with `isPublic`), and ready `read` args on every entry. NOTE: structure only — an outline is NOT a read of a symbol's body (use read_symbol/read_enclosing for that).
metadata.promptSnippet: Inspect a syntax-only ast-grep code outline.

paths.description: Files or directories to outline (workspace-relative or absolute).

lang.description: Restrict to one language. Required for stdin; for paths, ast-grep infers per file when omitted.

items.description: Which top-level items to include. auto = `structure` for a file, `exports` for a directory (default).

view.description: Text presentation level for the underlying outline; `expanded` shows members.

type.description: Keep only these symbol types, e.g. ["class","function"].

match.description: Keep only top-level items whose name matches this regex.

pubMembers.description: Show only public members in member views.

globs.description: Include/exclude file globs for directory input, e.g. ["*.ts","!**/dist/**"].

metadata.name: ast_grep_dump
metadata.label: AST-Grep Dump
metadata.description: Dump the tree-sitter AST for a source snippet using ast-grep CLI. Use when ast_grep_search returns zero matches and you need exact node kinds, field names, or nesting. Named nodes only by default; includeAnonymous=true shows punctuation/CST nodes too.
metadata.promptSnippet: Inspect AST node kinds before writing ast-grep patterns

source.description: Source code snippet to parse and dump

includeAnonymous.description: Show anonymous punctuation/CST nodes too (default false)

metadata.name: lsp_navigation
metadata.label: LSP Navigate
metadata.description:
Navigate code using LSP (Language Server Protocol). LSP is enabled by default; disable with --no-lsp.
Operations:
- definition: Jump to where a symbol is defined
- typeDefinition: Jump to the definition of a symbol's TYPE (e.g. the class/interface of a variable)
- declaration: Jump to a symbol's declaration (e.g. an extern/forward decl, distinct from its definition)
- references: Find all usages of a symbol
- hover: Get type/doc info at a position
- signatureHelp: Show callable signatures at cursor
- documentSymbol: List all symbols (functions/classes/vars) in a file
- findSymbol: Search document symbols in a file by name/detail with optional kind/top-level/exact filters
- workspaceSymbol: Search symbols across the whole project (best with path context)
- codeAction: Find available quick fixes/refactors at a range
- rename: Compute or apply workspace edits for renaming a symbol
- rename_file: Preview/apply LSP-aware source file rename notifications
- implementation: Jump to interface implementations
- prepareCallHierarchy: Get callable item at position (for incoming/outgoing)
- incomingCalls: Find all functions/methods that CALL this function
- outgoingCalls: Find all functions/methods CALLED by this function
- executeCommand: Run a server-advertised command via workspace/executeCommand. HARDENED: allowlisted to commands the server advertised; dry-run by default (reports whether advertised) — set apply:true to actually run. Pass command (+ optional commandArguments).
- workspaceDiagnostics: List all diagnostics tracked by active LSP clients
- capabilities: Show cached operation support for active LSP servers

Line and character are 1-based (as shown in editors). For position-based operations, prefer passing symbol when you know the line but not the exact character; character can be omitted or -1 and choco-pi-lsp will resolve the symbol column. Use symbol#N for repeated symbols on the same line (1-based occurrence).
metadata.promptSnippet: Find definitions, references, and hover info via LSP

operation.description: LSP operation to perform. Valid values: definition, typeDefinition, declaration, references, hover, signatureHelp, documentSymbol, findSymbol, workspaceSymbol, codeAction, rename, rename_file, implementation, prepareCallHierarchy, incomingCalls, outgoingCalls, executeCommand, workspaceDiagnostics, capabilities

path.description: Absolute or relative file path. Required for file-scoped operations; optional for workspaceSymbol/workspaceDiagnostics.

character.description: Character offset (1-based). Optional when symbol is provided; use -1 to force symbol-column resolution.

symbol.description: Symbol name on the target line for automatic character resolution. Use symbol#N to select the Nth occurrence on the line.

endLine.description: End line (1-based). Optional; used by codeAction range.

endCharacter.description: End character (1-based). Optional; used by codeAction range.

apply.description: rename/executeCommand: apply for real. rename defaults to preview; executeCommand defaults to a dry-run that only reports whether the command is advertised — set apply:true to actually run it.

command.description: executeCommand only: the server command id to run. Must be one the server advertised (see the capabilities operation).

commandArguments.description: executeCommand only: arguments array passed to workspace/executeCommand.

query.description: Symbol name to search. Used by workspaceSymbol and findSymbol.

kinds.description: findSymbol only: restrict matches to symbol kind labels such as function, class, method, variable, interface.

exactMatch.description: findSymbol only: match whole symbol names/details exactly instead of substring matching.

topLevelOnly.description: findSymbol only: do not search nested child symbols.

maxResults.description: findSymbol only: maximum matches to return. Default 20.

callHierarchyItem.description: Call hierarchy item. Required for incomingCalls/outgoingCalls

metadata.name: diagnostic_mark
metadata.label: Mark Diagnostic
metadata.description: Record a disposition for a diagnostics_report finding, using the exact filePath/rule/message/line it was reported with. false-positive/suppress persist across sessions; defer lasts only for the current session (resurfaces next time); flagged marks it for you to come back and fix, and shows up tagged in a later diagnostics_report mode=full. suppress additionally writes a `choco-pi-lsp-ignore: <rule>` comment into the source above the flagged line — rule is required for suppress. The line is verified/reanchored against current diagnostics before writing (#802): if a live diagnostic for this tool/rule/message is now at a different line, that line is used instead of the one you passed. When suppressing several findings in the SAME file in one turn, work bottom-up (highest line number first) — each inserted comment shifts later lines down by one, and reanchoring can't always disambiguate two nearby findings.
metadata.promptSnippet: Record a diagnostic disposition or deferred fix.

filePath.description: The file the diagnostic was reported on (relative or absolute).

line.description: The 1-based line the diagnostic was reported at.

message.description: The diagnostic's message, exactly as diagnostics_report reported it.

rule.description: The diagnostic's rule id, if it has one (shown in diagnostics_report as [rule]). Required for disposition=suppress.

tool.description: The tool that produced the diagnostic, if known.

disposition.description: false-positive = the rule misfired. suppress = real finding, won't fix (writes an inline ignore comment). defer = fix later, this session only. flagged = mark for you to fix.

reason.description: Optional short reason, kept alongside the disposition.

metadata.description: Toggle choco-pi-lsp on/off for the current session. Usage: /lens-toggle
Turn choco-pi-lsp LSP usage on or off at runtime, or show its state. Usage: /lsp on|off|status
Toggle automatic context injection on/off for the current session (tools/LSP/read-guard/formatting stay active). Usage: /lens-context-toggle
Show or hide the choco-pi-lsp diagnostics widget below the editor. Usage: /lens-widget-toggle
Show Technical Debt Index (TDI) and project health trend. Usage: /lens-tdi
Render the review graph as a self-contained interactive HTML project map (pan/zoom/hover/click) and write it to disk. Usage: /lens-map
Show choco-pi-lsp runtime health: pipeline crashes, slow runners, and last dispatch latency. Usage: /lens-health
Show the slowest latency-log phases by p50 and p99 for the current process session and machine-wide active log window. Usage: /lens-perf
Show choco-pi-lsp tool installation status: globally installed, auto-installed, or npx fallback. Usage: /lens-tools
Allow one edit to a file without a prior read. Usage: /lens-allow-edit <path>

options.description: Start choco-pi-lsp disabled for this session. Re-enable with /lens-toggle. Also via lens.enabled=false in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Disable unified LSP diagnostics and use language-specific fallbacks (for example pyright). Also via lsp.enabled=false in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Opt in to pre-starting a language server during session startup. Also via warmup.enabled=true in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json or CHOCO_PI_LSP_WARMUP=1.
Disable automatic formatting entirely (deferred format runs at agent_end by default). Also via format.enabled=false in config.
Run automatic formatting immediately after each write/edit instead of deferring to agent_end. Also via format.mode="immediate" in config.
Disable auto-fixing of lint issues (Biome, Ruff, ESLint). Also via autofix.enabled=false in config.
Disable test runner on write. Also via tests.enabled=false in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Disable delta mode (show all diagnostics, not just new ones). Also via delta.enabled=false in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Experimental: block git commit/push when unresolved choco-pi-lsp blockers exist. Also via guard.enabled=true in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.

Disable the Opengrep security scanner (a default-on auxiliary LSP; auto-installs, uses repo rules if present else the login-free 'auto' ruleset). Also via opengrep.enabled=false in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Disable read-before-edit behavior monitor. Also via readGuard.enabled=false in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.

Disable automatic context injection (session-start guidance, turn-end & test findings) while keeping tools, LSP, read-guard, and formatting active. Toggle with /lens-context-toggle. Also via contextInjection.enabled=false in config or CHOCO_PI_LSP_NO_CONTEXT_INJECTION=1.

Opt-in: persist a per-turn transcript entry summarizing diagnostics found, autofixes applied, and autoformats applied this turn (#484). Collapsed one-line, expandable in place. Default off. Also via turnSummary.enabled=true in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Write turn-delta fixable warning reports and inject a short advisory. Also via actionableWarnings.enabled=true in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Enrich actionable-warning reports with LSP code-action titles (requires an active language server). Also via actionableWarnings.includeLspCodeActions=true in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Experimental: apply conservative LSP quickfixes for actionable warnings at agent_end. Also via actionableWarnings.autoFix.enabled=true in config.
Report every actionable warning, not just those introduced this turn. Also via actionableWarnings.deltaOnly=false in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.

Opt-in (#1327): collapse a choco-pi-lsp tool's call+result rows into ONE theme-aware line (status glyph + name + summary) instead of two. Preserves expand-to-view-full-output. Default off. Also via ui.compactToolLine=true in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
Keep all choco-pi-lsp tools active to avoid tool-list cache changes. Also via tools.lazy=false in ~/.choco-pi-lsp/config.json.
